views.label: Inside the bubble

legend: the equator of the moment, which $\chi$ and $\phi$ cover whole
$\chi$ constant, every $1/2$, the circle of comoving observers at that $\chi$

views.settings: $\ell = \sqrt{-3/\Lambda}$, the curvature radius of the new vacuum, the unit of every length and of $c\tau$, and every length along a sheet measured with $dX^2 + dY^2 - dZ^2$.
views.input: A new vacuum of negative energy, $a = \ell\sin(c\tau/\ell)$, anti-de Sitter space inside the bubble.
stops: At every $\chi > 0$ the circles grow faster than the distance out to them, $g_{\chi\chi} < (\partial_\chi\sqrt{g_{\phi\phi}})^2$, and no surface of revolution in flat space carries the slice; Minkowski space carries it.
caption: The equatorial plane ($\theta = \pi/2$) of the open universe inside a bubble of negative vacuum energy as its proper time runs from $c\tau = \pi\ell/6$ to $5\pi\ell/6$, each moment drawn as a surface in three dimensional Minkowski space with every distance along it, measured with $dX^2 + dY^2 - dZ^2$, the metric distance. On it $g_{\chi\chi} = a^2$ while the circle at $\chi$ has circumference $2\pi a\sinh\chi$, so every circle grows faster than the distance out to it, and the moment is the hyperbolic plane of curvature $-1/a^2$. It lies whole on one sheet of the hyperboloid $Z^2 - X^2 - Y^2 = a^2$.

The sheet flattens as the universe grows to $a = \ell$ at $c\tau = \pi\ell/2$ and sharpens again as $a$ falls back toward zero at $c\tau = \pi\ell$. The circle of comoving observers at each $\chi$ has the radius $a\sinh\chi$, so the circles swell and shrink together, and each moment is infinite.
